report_summary.desc: Report a slice of compile progress (pages produced / contradictions auto-merged / pending), one sentence to one paragraph.

propose_plan.desc: Call after Plan-phase alignment: submit a short, readable, reviewable compile plan (the plan argument, markdown) for the owner's approval, then stop and wait. Do not write candidate/ pages before approval arrives.
propose_plan.ack: Plan submitted to the owner (the UI now shows the plan and the approve control); awaiting approval. Do not write candidate/ pages until the approval message arrives.
propose_plan.reminder: (Reminder: while you are at it, maintain the candidate-page list as `- [ ] page — one line` in the ## Next Pages section of authoring/PLAN.md as your working state, to make progress easy to track; this does not affect the plan you just submitted.)

delete_candidate_page.desc: Delete exactly one genuinely dead Markdown page below candidate/ after merging duplicate or orphan content. Pass a path relative to candidate/ (for example `guide/old.md`). This tool cannot delete index.md/log.md, directories, non-Markdown files, symlinks, or anything outside candidate/. Fix incoming links before deleting the page.
delete_candidate_page.markdown_only: only candidate Markdown pages may be deleted: {path}
delete_candidate_page.reserved: reserved routing pages cannot be deleted: {path}
delete_candidate_page.not_file: candidate path is not a regular file: {path}

resolve_ticket.desc: Call once per contradiction ticket you have patched (one call per ticket, no batching): register which ticket (ticket_id), the value you applied (applied_value), the candidate files you actually edited (pages_edited — must cover the ticket's affected_pages), and a one-line note. This marks the ticket as patched and writes an auditable agent_report — the basis for the contradiction view showing 'AI patched' for the owner to verify. Echo dispatch_nonce verbatim from the apply directive's `nonce:` line (empty string when the directive carries none) — it matches this receipt to the exact dispatch round.

exclude_source.desc: Declare that one raw source will NOT be compiled, or CORRECT an exclusion you already recorded. Pass `path` (relative to raw/, exact file path — no globs) and `reason` (one line the owner can understand, in the KB's language). The system validates the path against the source inventory, writes the exclusion ledger entry canonically, and de-duplicates. Calling it again for the same path with a different reason updates that row; with the same reason it is a no-op. Use remove_exclusion to lift an exclusion. These tools are the normal way to maintain authoring/EXCLUSIONS.json; editing that file by hand is permitted only as a last resort when no tool can express the fix, and the system re-canonicalizes the ledger after every turn either way.
exclude_source.not_in_inventory: not a raw source on record: {path}{hint}
exclude_source.already: already excluded with that same reason (nothing to do): {path}

remove_exclusion.desc: Lift an exclusion — use it when a source was excluded by mistake and should be compiled after all, or when a wrong row has to go. Pass `path`: the exact raw-relative source path, or, for a legacy hand-written row, that row's pattern string verbatim (for example `logs/**`). Matching is by exact pattern, never by what the pattern would match, so neighbouring rows are never taken out with it; it reports how many rows were removed. To only change an exclusion's REASON, call exclude_source again with the new reason instead.

report_domain.desc: One sentence naming the DOMAIN this knowledge base covers and the kind of question it can answer. It exists so another agent can decide whether to open this library at all — it is not an inventory, so do not list pages or count them. It matters most when the library's name is vague ("general knowledge base").
report_domain.need_args: domain is required: one sentence naming the field this library covers.
